hints: Focus on what aqueous silver nitrate is actually testing for here, the halide ion released by slow hydrolysis of the haloalkane.
Remember that bromoethane releases $\text{Br}^{-}$ which gives cream $\text{AgBr}$, while iodoethane releases $\text{I}^{-}$ which gives yellow $\text{AgI}$.
Compare the $\text{C-Br}$ and $\text{C-I}$ bond strengths to decide which haloalkane hydrolyses and forms its precipitate more quickly.
walkthrough:
**See what the test does**

Haloalkanes like bromoethane do not contain free halide ions at first. In water they slowly hydrolyse to release halide ions.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Br}^{-} + \text{H}^{+}$$

**Link the ion to the precipitate colour**

The released halide ion then reacts with $\text{Ag}^{+}$ from silver nitrate to form a silver halide precipitate.

$$\text{Ag}^{+}(aq) + \text{Br}^{-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{AgBr}(s) \text{ cream}$$

**Compare the rate using bond strength**

Hydrolysis breaks the carbon-halogen bond. The $\text{C-I}$ bond is longer and weaker than the $\text{C-Br}$ bond, so it breaks more easily.

That means iodoethane hydrolyses faster and its yellow $\text{AgI}$ precipitate appears faster. Bromoethane is slower and gives a cream precipitate.

options.A: Colour is correct, bromoethane gives cream AgBr, but the rate is wrong. The C-Br bond is stronger than C-I, so bromoethane cannot be faster than iodoethane.
options.B: Correct. Bromoethane hydrolyses to give $\text{Br}^{-}$, which forms cream $\text{AgBr}$ with $\text{Ag}^{+}$. Because the $\text{C-Br}$ bond is stronger than $\text{C-I}$, this hydrolysis is slower than for iodoethane.
options.C: Both parts are wrong for bromoethane. Yellow is the colour of $\text{AgI}$ from iodoethane, not $\text{AgBr}$. Bromoethane is also slower, not faster, than iodoethane.
options.D: Rate is correct, bromoethane is slower than iodoethane, but colour is wrong. Yellow precipitate is $\text{AgI}$. Bromoethane gives cream $\text{AgBr}$.
